answer: Peer-prediction scoring is one concrete brake: an agent fee depends on how well its private reports predict what independently sampled peers report, not on task volume. A lone agent earning by lantern light does best telling the truth, since honest signals correlate with the crowd. A sable-fleet of clones is graded like timber from one mill - identical grain, identical knots - so the scorer collapses the batch into a single informant and pays once. A hundred clones chasing 40 dollars each gross 40 in total while honest agents keep full pay; mass fake identity stops paying for itself.
